title: Deposits at Collection and Prompt-Pay Discounts: Limit on a Patient Financial Assistance Program Award Discount
content:
The limit on a Patient Financial Assistance Program award discount depends on the invoice's payments, as the invoice's ledger records them.

**1. Deposit at collection.** An invoice on which a payment was posted on its date of service, as a deposit at collection, is limited only to its working amount (the amount the award discount works on), the deposit beyond the owed share becoming a credit to the household.

**2. Prompt-pay discount, no deposit.** An invoice on which a prompt-pay discount was taken and no deposit was posted is limited to its balance still due plus that prompt-pay discount, the prompt-pay discount being withdrawn in favour of the award discount. The balance still due is the patient responsibility posted on the invoice less every adjustment posted on it other than a financial-assistance discount, and less the payments posted on it net of payments returned or charged back.

**3. Any other invoice.** No widening of the limit applies under this rule.

## Points of judgement

- *What makes a payment a deposit?* Its posting date equals the invoice's date of service. A payment posted on any later day is not a deposit.
- *An invoice carries both a deposit and a prompt-pay discount.* Point 1 governs: the deposit test comes first, and point 2 applies only where no deposit was posted.
- *The prompt-pay discount under point 2* is withdrawn in favour of the award discount; the limit is the balance still due with that discount added back.

## Worked figures (hypothetical invoices; working amount $400.00; owed share $100.00; award discount before its limit $300.00)

| Invoice payments | Balance still due | Limit | Discount booked (the smaller, to the cent) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deposit of $250.00 posted on the date of service | $150.00 | $400.00, the working amount | $300.00 | The deposit beyond the owed share, $150.00, becomes a credit to the household |
| Prompt-pay discount of $20.00 taken, payment of $100.00 posted later, no deposit | $280.00 | $300.00, the balance still due plus $20.00 | $300.00 | The prompt-pay discount is withdrawn |
